user: OK. What documents do I need to prepare for the dispute?
answer:
The knowledge base doesn't list the documents required for a goods-not-received dispute, so I can't tell you exactly what to prepare. I don't want to guess.

What I can confirm from the documentation:
- The window for a goods-not-received dispute is 90 days from the transaction date. The transaction was found eligible, so it is within that window.
- You can withdraw a dispute at any time before it is resolved. Withdrawal is final, and the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.

Some useful steps while you gather whatever evidence you have:
- Keep any order confirmation, receipt, or invoice for the purchase.
- Keep records of communication with the merchant about the delivery, such as emails or chat messages.
- Note the expected delivery date and any tracking information.

If you want, I can search the knowledge base again for the evidence requirements, or escalate to a human agent who can tell you exactly what to submit.

Nothing has been filed yet. I'll open the dispute only when you explicitly confirm that you want me to proceed.

fragments.text:
Notifications
## Dispute updates
A dispute generates a notification on every state change. The notification
names the state, never the internal reason for a decision.

Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each dispute reason code has its own window, counted in days from the
transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Dispute handling process
## Withdrawing a dispute
A customer may withdraw a dispute at any time before resolution. Withdrawal is
final; the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.

Regulatory framework
## Unauthorised transactions
A customer is liable for at most EUR 50 of losses from an unauthorised
transaction before it is reported, and for nothing after. This does not apply
where the customer acted fraudulently or with gross negligence.
